Wrestling with Doubt—Faith in the Face of Uncertainty.
You know, no matter how many incredible visions or miracles someone experiences, doubt still manages to sneak in. There are those days when the memories of heaven's light feel so far away, and the shadows of fear and skepticism seem to stretch on forever. Maybe you've wondered too—was it all just a dream? A trick of the mind? Or maybe just wishful thinking?
Here’s something I’ve learned: wrestling with doubt isn’t a weakness. It’s just part of being human.
I remember a time when it felt like God’s presence had faded into the background. My prayers felt empty, and all those old questions came rushing back. What if none of it was real? What if those visions were just my brain trying to cope with trauma? The urge to give up and slip into cynicism was honestly overwhelming.
But in those quiet, late-night moments, something shifted. A new kind of faith started to take root—not the faith that comes from seeing miracles, but the trust you choose, especially when things feel uncertain. It hit me: faith isn’t about having all the answers. It’s about holding on to hope, right in the middle of your doubts.
Most people think faith is a feeling, but more often, it’s a decision. It’s that daily choice to trust, to keep moving forward, even when you can’t see what’s ahead.
One night, as I lay awake wrestling with those doubts, a memory floated up—a moment from one of my near-death experiences, when I felt pure love and acceptance. That memory was enough to quiet my fears, at least for a little while.
It became clear: the journey of faith isn’t a straight path. It’s winding, full of ups and downs.
And the struggle with doubt never fully disappears. But over time, it becomes less scary. It’s not something I’m ashamed of anymore. In fact, it’s almost like a companion on this journey.
I realized that these experiences with death and the afterlife weren’t meant to erase every question. Instead, they’re a foundation of hope—something steady enough to withstand the storms of life.
So, here’s the key takeaway: faith isn’t about certainty. It’s about trust. And even in your darkest moments, there’s a light that just can’t be put out.
